title: Protocol for the preparation of site-specific succinylated histone mimics to investigate the impact on nucleosome dynamics
protocol: Dissolve succinic anhydride, N-hydroxysuccinimide, and DMAP in toluene.
Add triethylamine and tert-butyl alcohol to the mixture.
Reflux the mixture for 24 hours.
Cool the mixture to 25°C.
Wash the upper organic phase with 1 M HCl solution.
Wash the organic phase with brine.
Dry the organic phase over Na₂SO₄.
Filter the dried organic phase.
Concentrate under vacuum to give the crude product.
Purify the crude product using flash chromatography.
Elute the column with 9:1 DCM/acetone.
Afford the product as a yellow oil.
Dissolve mono-tert-butyl succinate (500 mg, 2.87 mmol), NH4Cl (3.0 eq, 460.59 mg, 8.61 mmol), EDCI (1.5 eq, 825.38 mg, 4.31 mmol), and HOBt (1.5 eq, 659.35 mg, 4.31 mmol) in 10 mL DMF.
Add DIEA (1.5 eq, 556.47 mg, 4.31 mmol) to the mixture.
Stir the reaction solution for 6 h at 25°C.
Pour the reaction solution into 30 mL saturated NaHCO3 solution and extract with ethyl acetate (3 × 20 mL).
Wash the combined organic layers with brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under vacuum.
Purify the crude product in a flash chromatography column eluted with 9:1 DCM/MeOH to afford tert-butyl succinamate as a clear oil (497.18 mg, 2.87 mmol, 100% yield).

Dissolve tert-butyl succinamate (100 mg, 0.577 mmol), Cs2CO3 (1.0 eq, 188.10 mg, 0.577 mmol), CuI (0.2 eq, 21.99 mg, 0.115 mmol), vinyl iodide (0.8 eq, 71.10 mg, 0.462 mmol), and N1,N2-dimethylethane-1,2-diamine (0.4 eq, 20.36 mg, 0.230 mmol) in 5 mL anhydrous THF.
Stir the reaction mixture for 17 h at 70°C under argon protection.
Filter the reaction mixture.
Concentrate the filtrate under vacuum to afford the crude product.
Purify the crude product in a flash chromatography column eluted with 50:50 hexane/ethyl acetate.
Grow E. coli Rosetta cells harboring pET-histone expression plasmids in 1 L LB media containing ampicillin and chloramphenicol at 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.8.
Add isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) to a final concentration of 0.6 mM.
Incubate for 4 h at 37°C.
Collect the cells by centrifugation at 3,500 × g for 25 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells in lysis buffer (25 mM HEPES, 1 mM EDTA, 1 M NaCl, pH 7.5).
Add 1 mM PMSF just before use to the lysis buffer.
Sonicate the cells for 5 seconds on and 10 seconds off for a total of 30 minutes.
Collect the inclusion body pellet by centrifugation at 4°C at 12,000 × g for 15 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 15 mL lysis buffer containing 1% Triton X-100.
Centrifuge the suspension at 12,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C and pour off the supernatant.
Repeat step f twice.
Wash the pellet twice with 15 mL lysis buffer.
After final wash, pour off the supernatant.
Add 250 μL DMSO to the pellet and incubate for 20 minutes at 25°C.
Add 5 mL HU-500 buffer (6 M Urea, 25 mM HEPES, 1 mM EDTA, 500 mM NaCl, pH 7.5) to the mixture.
Dilute the salt concentration from 500 mM to 100 mM by adding HU-0 buffer and shake for another 2 hours at 25°C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 20,000 × g for 10 minutes at 25°C.
Collect the supernatant and load it onto a HiTrap SP HP column (5 mL) pre-equilibrated with HU-100 buffer.
Elute histone proteins using a gradient of 0% to 100% HU-500 buffer over 25 minutes at a flow rate of 2 mL/min.
Analyze the eluted fractions by 18% SDS-PAGE.
Pool the fractions containing purified histone proteins.
Load the combined fractions onto a HiLoad 16/60 Superdex 200 pg size-exclusion column pre-equilibrated with HU-1000 buffer.
Elute histone proteins using 100% HU-1000 buffer at a flow rate of 2 mL/min.
Analyze peak fractions by 18% SDS-PAGE and collect corresponding fractions.
Dialyze histone proteins against dd H2O containing 2 mM DTT at 4°C (at least three changes).
Freeze dry the protein solution to obtain lyophilized histone powder.
Dissolve mutated histone H2BK34C in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) containing 6 M Gdn·HCl to a final concentration of 1 mM.
Add DTT to the solution to achieve a final concentration of 5 mM.
Prepare a fresh DTT stock solution at 1 M.
Add 50 equivalent (50 mM) of compound 1 into the reaction mixture.
Add VA-044 to the reaction mixture at a final concentration of 20 mM.
Add dimethyl sulfide to the reaction mixture at a final concentration of 100 mM.
Incubate the reaction tube in a 42°C water bath for 2 hours.
Analyze the reaction by LC-MS using a Vydac 218TP C4 column (4.6 mm × 250 mm).
Load the reaction mixture onto a semi-prep column (Vydac C4 column) after completion according to HPLC analysis.
Elute modified histone with a gradient of 20%–50% HPLC buffer B over 35 minutes.
Analyze peak fractions by ESI-MS and obtain deconvolution results in UniDec software.
Pool the fractions containing pure modified histones.
Lyoophilize the pooled fractions to dryness.
Store purified histone proteins at -80°C for an indefinite length of time.
Dissolve the intermediate protein H2BKc34succ-tBu in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) containing 6 M Gdn·HCl to a final concentration of 5 mM.
Keep the above protein solution on ice.
Add TFA dropwise to the reaction mixture to a final concentration of 70% (v/v).
Incubate the reaction at 25°C with shaking.
Monitor the reaction by LC-MS using a Vydac 218TP C4 column and ESI-MS.
Remove the TFA under a stream of compressed argon after reaction completion according to HPLC analysis.
Load the reaction mixture onto a semi-prep column (Vydac C4 column).
Elute deprotected histone with a gradient of 20%–50% HPLC buffer B over 35 min.
Analyze peak fractions by ESI-MS and obtain the deconvolution results using UniDec software.
Pool the fractions containing pure deprotected histones.
Lyophilize pooled fractions.
Mix equal molar quantities of H2A and H2B proteins in histone unfolding buffer (6 M Gdn·HCl, 20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 1.0 mM EDTA, 10 mM DTT) to a final histone concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min on ice.
Dialyze the mixture in histone refolding buffer (2 M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 1.0 mM EDTA, 5 mM β-mercaptoethanol) for 4 h at 4°C.
Change the histone refolding buffer and dialyze for another 16 h.
Concentrate the refolded dimer solution using an Amicon® Ultra 15 mL centrifugal filter device (Membrane nominal molecular weight limit, 3 kDa) to less than 1 mL.
Do not concentrate the total volume below 200 μL when performing concentration with the centrifugal filter device.
Load the concentrated mixture onto a HiLoad 16/60 Superdex 200 pg column pre-equilibrated with histone refolding buffer.
Elute histone proteins with histone refolding buffer over 25 min at a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Analyze peak fractions by 18% SDS-PAGE to verify the quality of purified dimers and pool corresponding fractions.
Concentrate pooled fractions using an Amicon® Ultra 15 mL centrifugal filter device with a nominal molecular weight limit of 3 kDa.
Dialyze concentrated fraction in storage buffer (2 M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA, 5 mM β-mercaptoethanol, 50% glycerol) for long-term storage.
Determine the protein concentration of assembled H2A-H2B dimers by Bradford Protein Assay kit.
Store assembled H2A-H2B dimers at −20°C.
Use the same method to prepare H2A-H2BKc34succ dimers and (H3-H4)2 tetramers.
Determine the protein concentration of the assembled histone dimers and (H3-H4)2 tetramers by Bradford Protein Assay kit.
Determine the concentration of fluorophore-labeled DNA by a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.

Mix purified histone dimers, (H3-H4)2 tetramers, and fluorophore-labeled "Widom 601" DNA at a molar ratio of dimer : tetramer : DNA = 2 : 1 : 1.2 to achieve a concentration of 2 μM in reconstitution buffer.
Test the ratio of dimer, tetramer, and DNA at a lower concentration (∼30 nM) in 30 μL to confirm nucleosome formation.
Transfer the mixture into a Slide-A-Lyzer MINI dialysis unit.
Dialyze the mixture sequentially against reconstitution buffers containing decreasing KCl concentrations for 50 min each: 1.6 M, 1.4 M, 1.2 M, 1.0 M, 0.8 M, 0.5 M, and 0.2 M KCl.
Dialyze the mixture in 10 mM KCl for 12 hours.
Check the quality and compaction of the reconstituted nucleosomes by Native-PAGE using a 5% TBE gel with acrylamide : Bis = 29 : 1.
Stain the Native-PAGE gel with ethidium bromide for 15 minutes.
Visualize the nucleosomes under UV using a MyECL Imager system.
Concentrate the reconstitution mixture to 75 μL using an EMD Millipore Amicon Ultra Centrifugal Filter.
Add 25 μL native loading buffer (62.5 mM Tris-HCl, pH 6.8, 40% glycerol, 0.01% Bromophenol Blue) to the concentrated mixture.
Purify the reconstituted nucleosomes by Native-PAGE using a mini prep cell with a 5% TBE gel and acrylamide : Bis = 60 : 1.
Monitor the elutant by UV spectrometer during purification.
Elution buffer contains 10 mM KCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl, 10% glycerol, pH 7.8, and 0.1 mM EDTA.
Running buffer contains 0.2× TBE for the purification process.
Analyze peak fractions by Native-PAGE using a 5% TBE gel with acrylamide : Bis = 29 : 1.
Pool corresponding fractions based on analysis results.
Concentrate purified nucleosomes using an Amicon® Ultra 15 mL centrifugal filter device with a nominal molecular weight limit of 3 kDa.
Determine the concentration of purified nucleosomes by UV-Vis spectrophotometer at A260 nm using NanoDrop 2000, Thermo.
Store the purified nucleosomes at 4°C until use.
Determine the concentration of purified nucleosomes by UV-Vis spectrophotometer at A260 nm using NanoDrop 2000, Thermo.
Dilute the purified nucleosomes in elution buffer to a final concentration of 1 ng/μL nucleosome.
Use a pipette to homogenize the mixture during FRET sample preparation.
Prepare FRET low salt buffer according to the specified composition.
Prepare FRET high salt buffer according to the specified composition.
Dilute nucleosome solution as required for the experiment.
Add 190 μL of experimental buffers at different salt concentrations from 0.01 M to 1.6 M.
Add 10 μL of diluted nucleosome solution into each buffer sample.
Incubate samples in a 384-well microplate (50 μL/well) for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Measure fluorescence intensity in each well using a plate reader.
Correct the intensity of donor and transfer channels as per the given equations.
Input the data into OriginPro 8 using salt concentration as the x-axis and FRET intensity as the y-axis.
Fit a sigmoidal function to the experimental curve.
Measure the stability of mononucleosomes by determining the c1/2 parameter.
c1/2 is the salt concentration where the intensity has dropped to half its initial value.
